error.generic: I could not complete it. Check the server log: the detail is there.

recordTransaction.noAccounts: The household has no account set up
recordTransaction.defaultedAccount: You did not say which account, so I charged it to {account}.

toAccountNotTransfer.head: "to_account" is the DESTINATION account of a transfer, and this is {kind, select, income {an income} other {an expense}}, not a transfer.
toAccountNotTransfer.hint: If "{sent}" is the account the money {kind, select, income {came into} other {went out of}}, send it in "account".
toAccountNotTransfer.retry: Repeat the call with account and without to_account or to_amount.

recordTransaction.transferNeedsDestination: A transfer needs a destination account
recordTransaction.sameAccount: The transfer's origin and destination are the same account
recordTransaction.categoryNotRecognised: I did not recognise the category "{input}"; I left it uncategorised for you to review.
recordTransaction.categoryUnsure: I read "{input}" as {category}, but I am not sure.
recordTransaction.currencyMismatch: The amount comes in {amountCurrency} but the account {account} carries {accountCurrency}. If you changed money from one currency to another, that is a transfer between accounts.
recordTransaction.noRate: I could not get the day's rate, so I saved it without the dollar equivalent. It is flagged for review.
recordTransaction.staleRate: I used the rate from {date} because there was none for today.
recordTransaction.accountUnsure: I read "{input}" as {account}, but I am not sure.

when.minutesAgo: {n, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} ago

duplicate.head: That is already recorded: «{description}» for {amount} in {account}, {when}. I did not duplicate it.
duplicate.noCent: Shifting the amount by a few cents does not get past this, it lands here just the same.
duplicate.allow: If it really is a different purchase, repeat the call with allow_duplicate: true.
duplicate.amend: If what you want is to change the one that already exists — the account, the category, the amount — use planfly_amend with target: "{id}" and the new field in the same call.
duplicate.warn: Careful: {when} I recorded an identical entry in the same account ({description}).

recordTransaction.transferNeedsToAmount: The transfer goes from {from} to {to}: tell me how much arrived in {account}.
recordTransaction.itemsNeedReview: There are products I did not fully recognise; they are left for review.
recordTransaction.itemsExceedTotal: The products add up to {amount}, more than the receipt's total.

summary.entry: {kind, select, expense {Expense} income {Income} other {Adjustment}} of {amount}{equivalent}{category} {kind, select, income {to} other {from}} {account}
summary.alreadyStored: I already had it recorded, I did not duplicate it.

recordTransaction.payeeNotRecognised: I do not know the place «{input}». The entry is recorded and waiting in the review tray for you to say which shop it was.

updateTransaction.notFound: I did not find that entry
updateTransaction.voided: That entry is voided, and a voided one is not edited: it stays in the history as a record of what happened. If you need it, record it again.
updateTransaction.notEditable: I did not find that entry among the ones I can correct (only the ones I recorded myself, from the last 7 days).
updateTransaction.malformed: That entry has no origin line
updateTransaction.accountCurrencyMismatch: {account} carries {accountCurrency} and the line is in {legCurrency}. If it really was that account, tell me the amount in {accountCurrency} too: an account's balance cannot mix currencies.
updateTransaction.notATransferAccount: That entry is not a transfer, it has no destination account. If what you want is to change the account it came out of, send it in "account", not in "to_account".
updateTransaction.sameAccount: Origin and destination would end up being the same account: that is not a transfer.
updateTransaction.notATransferAmount: That entry is not a transfer: it has only one line, so there is no destination amount.
updateTransaction.sameCurrencyAmounts: Both accounts are in the same currency, so what goes out and what comes in have to be the same figure.
updateTransaction.transferHasNoCategory: That entry is a transfer between your own accounts, and those carry no category: it is not an expense, you only moved the money.
updateTransaction.categoryNotFound: I did not find the category "{input}".
updateTransaction.notATransferRate: That entry is not a transfer: there is no destination line to put a rate on.
updateTransaction.itemsWithCurrencyChange: I cannot change the currency and the breakdown at once: the prices on screen are in the previous currency. Change the currency, save, and correct the breakdown afterwards.
updateTransaction.zeroItemTotal: The line "{description}" has no amount. A line at zero says nothing about any price.

warning.noRate: I have no rate from {date} for {currency}, so that line is left with no equivalent in {base}.
warning.staleRate: The nearest rate to {date} is from another day.
warning.rateIgnored: {leg, select, to {destination rate} other {rate}}: that line is already in {base}, no rate is needed. I ignored it.
warning.itemsNeedReview: There are products I did not fully recognise; it is left for review.
warning.itemsExceedTotal: The products add up to {amount}, more than the entry.
warning.leftUnvalued: It stays flagged for review until it has a rate.

change.valuation: {leg, select, to {destination valuation} other {valuation}} to the {source, select, bcv {official} p2p {parallel} other {manually set}} rate
change.items: breakdown to {n, plural, one {# product} other {# products}}

updateTransaction.payeeNotFound: I do not know the place «{input}». Add it in Places first, or leave it empty.

financing.missingRate: I have no {source} rate from {date} to turn the price from {from} into {to}.
financing.invalidInstallmentCount: The number of installments has to be a whole number greater than zero.
financing.financierNotFound: I found no account resembling "{input}". Create it first in Accounts, as a credit card or a loan.
financing.financierNotLiability: {account} is an asset account, and whoever finances you is who you owe. Change its type to credit card or loan in Accounts.
financing.downPaymentTooLarge: The deposit cannot be larger than the purchase's total.
financing.nothingToFinance: If the deposit covers everything, there is nothing to finance: record it as an ordinary expense.
financing.missingDownPaymentAccount: Tell me which account the deposit came out of.
financing.purchaseSummary: {description}: {total} in {financier}{downPayment}. {n, plural, one {# installment} other {# installments}} of {installment} left, the first one on {firstDue}
financing.installmentNotFound: I did not find that installment.
financing.unpaidWithVoid: Installment {number} is pending again, and I voided the transfer of {amount} that paid it. It stays in the history, flagged.
financing.accountNotFound: I did not find that account.
financing.profileNotLiability: {account} is an asset account. A financier is somebody you owe, so it has to be of type credit card or loan.
financing.invalidPercent: The deposit percentage has to be between 0 and 99.
financing.profileRemoved: It leaves the list of financiers. The account is still there.
financing.planNotFound: I did not find that purchase.
financing.planVoided: {description} voided, along with {n, plural, one {its entry} other {its # entries}}. They stay in the history, flagged.
financing.financedNote: Financed over {n, plural, one {# installment} other {# installments}}
financing.installmentPaidWithInterest: Installment {number} of {plan} paid: {amount}, of which {interest} is interest.

recurring.missingRate: I have no {source} rate from {date} to go from {from} to {to}.

announce.recorded: {n, plural, one {I recorded one recurrence} other {I recorded # recurrences}}
announce.failed: {n, plural, one {There is one I could not record} other {There are # I could not record}}

recurring.noDays: Pick at least one day of the month: the 5th, the 20th, the last one…
recurring.noNextRun: With those days there is no next date.
recurring.ruleNotFound: I did not find that recurrence.
recurring.created: «{name}» is set up. The next one, on {next}
recurring.paused: «{name}» paused. It will record nothing until you resume it.
recurring.removed: «{name}» deleted. What it already recorded stays in the history.

manageAccounts.duplicateArchived: There is already an archived account called "{name}". Rename the new one, or unarchive that one.
manageAccounts.duplicateName: You already have an account called "{name}".
manageAccounts.accountNotFound: I did not find that account.
manageAccounts.currencyLocked: {account} has {n, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} in {currency}, so its currency can no longer be changed: the amounts inside would stop meaning what they say. Create another account in {wanted} and transfer the balance.
manageAccounts.notEmpty: {account} has {amount}. Archiving it would take that money out of net worth with no entry to explain it. Transfer the balance to another account first.
manageAccounts.archived: {account} archived. Its entries are still there.
manageAccounts.unknownCurrency: I do not know the currency {currency}. The ones this planfly has are: {known}. An account in a currency that is not the money inside it makes every figure it touches false, so I would rather not open it than open it in another one.

manageCategories.duplicateArchived: There is already an archived category called "{name}". Rename the new one, or unarchive that one.
manageCategories.duplicateName: You already have a category called "{name}".
manageCategories.duplicateAlias: "{alias}" is already another name for {name}. Two categories answering to the same word makes the bot choose between them alphabetically, and the expenses would land in whichever sorts first.
manageCategories.categoryNotFound: I did not find that category.
manageCategories.ownParent: A category cannot hang from itself.
manageCategories.parentOtherKind: {parent} is a {kind} category, so nothing of another kind can hang from it: its total would add up two different things.
manageCategories.parentIsChild: {parent} already hangs from another category. Categories go two levels deep and no more, because that is as far as a budget looks.
manageCategories.parentArchived: {parent} is archived. Unarchive it first, or the category would hang off something that is not on the list.
manageCategories.hasChildren: {name} has categories hanging from it, so it cannot hang from another one: that would make a third level, which no budget looks at.
manageCategories.kindLocked: {name} carries {n, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} as a {kind} category, so that can no longer be changed: all of them would leave the month's total at a stroke, with nothing on screen to say where they went.
manageCategories.hasActiveChildren: {name} has {n, plural, one {# category} other {# categories}} hanging from it. Archive those first, or they would hang off something that is not on the list.
manageCategories.hasBudget: {name} has a budget in force. Remove it first, or it would keep counting against a category you can no longer see.
manageCategories.archived: {name} archived. Its entries are still there.

managePayees.duplicateArchived: There is already an archived place called "{name}". Rename the new one, or unarchive that one.
managePayees.duplicateName: You already have a place called "{name}".
managePayees.duplicateAlias: "{alias}" is already another name for {name}. Two places answering to the same word makes the bot choose between them alphabetically, and one shop's price history would end up split in two.
managePayees.taxIdArchived: {name} carries the fiscal id {taxId} and is archived. Unarchive it rather than writing it again, or its purchases would end up under two names.
managePayees.payeeNotFound: I did not find that place.
managePayees.categoryNotFound: I did not find that category.
managePayees.ownParent: A place cannot be a branch of itself.
managePayees.parentIsBranch: {parent} is already a branch of another place. A chain goes two levels and no more, because that is as far as its total looks.
managePayees.parentArchived: {parent} is archived. Unarchive it first, or the branch would hang off something that is not on the list.
managePayees.hasBranches: {name} has branches of its own, so it cannot become one: that would make a third level, which no total looks at.
managePayees.createdWithCategory: Place {name} created, filed under {category} by default.
managePayees.createdBranch: Place {name} created as a branch of {parent}.
managePayees.archived: {name} archived. Its purchases and their prices are still there.
managePayees.taxIdSameSpot: {name} already carries the fiscal id {taxId} at that same address. It is the shop you already have: a second row would split its price history in half, and neither half would tell you what anything costs.
managePayees.taxIdOtherSpot: {name} carries the fiscal id {taxId}, at another address. That reads like a second branch of the same company, which is a thing that happens — say so and I will keep both, and hang this one off its brand so their totals still add up together.
managePayees.placed: {n, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} now bought at {name}.

products.noText: The line has no text to identify a product by
products.mergeWithItself: A product cannot be merged with itself
products.oneNotFound: I did not find one of the two products
products.splitNoText: That line item has no text to name a product by
products.notFound: I did not find that product
products.isTheName: «{text}» is this product's name, not a line item that can be taken out of it.
products.noMatchingLines: No line of {product} says «{text}». Split by the text exactly as it came out on the receipt.
products.allItsLines: «{text}» is all of its lines: splitting it would leave {product} empty. That is renaming it, not splitting it.
products.split: {n, plural, one {# purchase moved} other {# purchases moved}} from {from} to {to}.

budgets.categoryNotFound: I did not find the category "{input}".
budgets.unknownPeriod: That kind of period does not exist.
budgets.missingRange: Tell me which day the budget runs from and which day it runs to.
budgets.endBeforeStart: The end date falls before the start date.
budgets.removed: {n, plural, one {I removed {category}'s budget.} other {I removed {category}'s # budgets.}}

rules.missingPattern: The rule needs some text to look for.
rules.categoryNotFound: I did not find the category "{input}".
rules.saved: Done: whatever contains «{pattern}» will be filed under {category}.

installmentReminders.heading: {n, plural, one {You have one installment to pay:} other {You have # installments to pay:}}

common.entryNotFound: I did not find that entry

rates.stillInUse: That rate has already valued {n, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}}, so it is not deleted: they would be left with their equivalent computed and no way of saying where it came from. Set another one for the same day and this one stops being used.

session.readOnly: This account is read-only: it cannot change anything.

items.unreadable: I could not read the breakdown the form sent.
items.notAList: The breakdown has to be a list of lines.
items.noDescription: Line {n} has an amount but does not say what it is.

actions.missingFinancierName: Tell me the name of whoever finances you.

rates.noSources: There is no source set up: write the day's rate below.
rates.oneWithoutSource: Updated. {source} has no source set up: write it below.
rates.bothBroken: Neither of the two sources answered.
rates.manualSaved: {slot, select, bcv {The official one} other {The parallel one}} for {date} is now {rate} · that day's entries are valued with it.
rates.removed: Rate deleted. Send the source's again, if there is one.

actions.ruleRemoved: Rule deleted. What it already categorised stays as it is.
actions.accountNotFound: I did not find the account "{name}".
actions.missingEntry: The entry to correct is missing.
actions.missingAccount: The account to correct is missing.
actions.missingCategory: The category to correct is missing.
actions.missingPayee: The place to correct is missing.

amount.head: I could not read the amount {input}: {reason}
amount.notFinite: it is not a finite number
amount.badExpression: it is not a sum that can be worked out
amount.empty: it came out empty once cleaned up
amount.badCharacters: it contains characters that are neither digits nor separators
amount.notAnInteger: the digits do not form a valid integer
amount.rateHead: I could not read the rate {input}: {reason}
amount.rateBadCharacters: a rate carries only digits and separators
amount.rateAmbiguous: I cannot tell whether the dot separates thousands or decimals. Write it with a decimal comma ({suggestion}) or with no thousands separator
amount.rateTooPrecise: it does not fit the rates column
amount.rateTooHigh: it is too high to be a rate (more than {max})

manageCurrencies.badCode: A currency code is two to six letters: USD, VES, COP.
manageCurrencies.symbolFixed: {code} will print as «{symbol}»: the formatting keeps its own list of symbols and falls back to the code, so one typed here would be stored and never shown. Leave it empty.
manageCurrencies.notFound: I do not know the currency {code}.
manageCurrencies.inUse: {code} has {n, plural, one {# account} other {# accounts}} in it. Move or archive them before removing the currency: everything recorded in it is written with its decimals.
manageCurrencies.created: {code} added. An account can be opened in it now.

change.name: the name
change.hasOfficial: it now has an official rate
change.noOfficial: it now has one rate only
